tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before performing a move, verify that the chosen disk is the topmost disk on its source peg and that the source peg actually contains that disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you select a disk to move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 from peg 1 while disk 2 sits on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints; use it to temporarily hold a peg clear for moving larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk is blocked by smaller disks on its source or destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 1 onto peg 0 to free disk 5 for a later move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the largest disks in the correct order, keep them untouched and build the remaining tower on top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the target peg already has a correctly ordered stack of larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving disk 5 on peg 2 while moving smaller disks onto it later.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Assemble the final tower by handling disks from largest to smallest, placing each disk onto its goal peg after clearing any obstacles.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Throughout the solution, after clearing smaller disks, move the next largest disk to its final position.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 before moving disk 4, then disk 3, etc.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full sequence of moves, output it as the last syntactically correct list in the response, with no extra text after it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of the reasoning, before the final answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing commentary after the move list, causing the parser to miss the list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Ensure source and destination pegs are clear of smaller disks before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk, make sure its source peg has no smaller disks on top and its destination peg is empty or has a larger top disk; use the smallest disk as a buffer to relocate any blocking disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you plan to move a disk that is not the smallest.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 onto peg 0 while disk 1 sits on top of peg 0.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Limit move list length to stay within token limits
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a concise solution, preferably using the optimal or near‑optimal sequence of moves, to keep the move list short enough to fit within the model’s output token budget.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move sequence, aim for minimal or near‑minimal moves.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Producing an excessively long move list that gets truncated by the verifier.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model finishes its reasoning without emitting the required final list, often due to forgetting the output format.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always conclude the response with a syntactically correct move list and no trailing text.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving the desired disk without checking the top disk on the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk based on its target location but neglects to ensure it is the topmost on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The generated move sequence exceeds the model’s token budget, causing the final list to be cut off.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Prefer concise, near‑optimal sequences and monitor token usage; keep the move list short enough to fit.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model mis‑tracks the current state, assuming a disk is on a peg when it has already been moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an explicit mental representation of the current configuration after each move.
